decision: 2024 national sales: no figure is used
evidence_in_brief: Department has published nothing after 2023. FIASA is not used as a source (8 October). Road Accident Fund levy: 24.25 and 24.42 bn litres of both fuels in the years to March 2024 and 2025
analyst_proposal: Start the forecast from 2023, the last year with department sales; leave 2024 blank

decision: Customs as the trade source from 2014
evidence_in_brief: Balance rebuilt on SARS; a test checks every year against the extract; FIASA kept as a comparison
analyst_proposal: Accept

decision: Treatment of 2018 and 2019 where customs is below FIASA
evidence_in_brief: No missing month, tariff line or unit problem; UN Comtrade agrees with customs; FIASA and the 2018 energy balance share one earlier reading
analyst_proposal: Keep customs; likely a later revision but not proven

decision: How to describe the diesel gap
evidence_in_brief: Four indicative comparisons plus the Road Accident Fund levy point to 2-4 bn litres above recorded sales; production, stocks and periods are unmatched
analyst_proposal: Hypothesis to test; not added to demand

decision: Treatment of the 2014 and 2018 provincial differences
evidence_in_brief: Provincial sum is above the national file by 0.13-0.14 bn litres in 2014; below it by 0.21-0.22 in 2018, where the quarter 1 district sheet is missing districts. From 8 October the provincial data is the main series and is used as published
analyst_proposal: Provincial figures stand as published; or scale the one faulty quarter in each year to the national total

decision: 39 replacement values in the diesel jet and petrol tables
evidence_in_brief: Each lever has an observed baseline; replacements for road freight, rail diversion, aircraft movements, fuel per movement, mileage, GDP growth, battery electric share and yields
analyst_proposal: Accept or challenge value by value

decision: Nine levers added by the analyst
evidence_in_brief: Real diesel and petrol price, private backup generation, electric share of new trucks and light commercial vehicles (benchmarked on Brazil, India and Europe), plug-in and conventional hybrids, rail passengers, exports to neighbours; two are well anchored, two are weak
analyst_proposal: Include in scenario design; treat backup generation and hybrids as weak

decision: Secunda utilisation
evidence_in_brief: Capacity corrected to 150 thousand barrels a day with utilisation re-based so output is unchanged; model gives 62 for 2024, Sasol reports 80
analyst_proposal: Raise utilisation to match reported output

decision: Reference case
evidence_in_brief: No medium case is agreed; medium values are proposals
analyst_proposal: Agree after the ranges

decision: Agriculture and industry starting values
evidence_in_brief: 2021 energy balance: 1.06 and 1.50 bn litres, against placeholders of 0.70 and 2.50; lowers 2024 diesel by 0.63 bn litres. Mining output is 7% lower in 2024 than 2021
analyst_proposal: Accept both as provisional; or 1.40 for industry

decision: Power generation starting value
evidence_in_brief: Model has 3.58 bn litres for 2024; Eskom reports 0.68-0.94 and all plants about 1.6 in the peak year
analyst_proposal: Recalibrate to reported burn at 0.31 litres per kWh

decision: Allowance for on-road use inside agriculture and mining diesel
evidence_in_brief: No published source sizes it; 20% would be about 0.47 bn litres; Road Accident Fund rebates cover 1.46 bn litres across all rebated sectors
analyst_proposal: None applied; ask SARS for refund data by sector

decision: Whether ships' diesel sits inside the inland diesel total
evidence_in_brief: Model carries 0.77 bn litres of marine gas oil; no observed figure
analyst_proposal: Decide scope before reconciling to sales

decision: Whether to calibrate mining and manufacturing on the energy balance
evidence_in_brief: Mining diesel per index point ranges 11-17 million litres between years; manufacturing lines are absent before 2016
analyst_proposal: Use a multi-year average and hold intensity; mark as provisional

decision: Provisional monthly turns
evidence_in_brief: Lesedi 1 / 2 / 2.4 and Durban 1 / 2 / 3 on operational capacity; Vopak's stated Durban target was 2-3
analyst_proposal: Agree as provisional ranges

decision: Apply turns to operational fuel capacity instead of gross capacity
evidence_in_brief: Lesedi 124,000 of 140,000 m3; Durban 146,000 fuel of 360,246 m3 gross
analyst_proposal: Change the pack's handling page

decision: Send the data request to Vopak
evidence_in_brief: Eight values marked to confirm with client; Vopak's website publishes no operating data
analyst_proposal: Send now

decision: Provincial sales for 2023
evidence_in_brief: Six methods back-tested; quarter 1 2023 shares are best (2.5 share points misallocated for petrol, 5.3 for diesel). 2024 and 2025 are blank: there is no department national total to split
analyst_proposal: Use as labelled estimates; ask the department for district data

decision: Source selection in the demand workbook
evidence_in_brief: Set to Department for 2022-2023 in the extended copy. The added sheets use no FIASA figure; 2024 on Nigel's own sheet is still set to FIASA
analyst_proposal: Accept; decide what Nigel's sheet should show for 2024 now that FIASA is not used

decision: Committing the remaining original files
evidence_in_brief: Nigel committed the refresh originals on main on 7 October
analyst_proposal: Closed

decision: Marine baseline elasticities and road parameters
evidence_in_brief: Carried over from 6 October; no new evidence
analyst_proposal: Unchanged

decision: Power fleet: the three cases and the assumptions behind them
evidence_in_brief: Fleet defined: Ankerlig Gourikwa Avon Dedisa (3,089 MW). Low / medium / high give 20 / 637 / 4,224 million litres from 2031. Unsourced: 10% of output on diesel when gas is available; 40% load factor on gas; 0.31 litres per kWh; Avon and Dedisa continuing after 2030-2031; 6 GW of gas turbines sited at Camden Grootvlei Hendrina Arnot and Kriel; no gas reaching them in the high case
analyst_proposal: Accept the fleet; confirm or change each case setting; replaces the two placeholder stations in the model

decision: Production after 2021: no figure is used
evidence_in_brief: Department energy balances end at 2021; all fifteen files re-downloaded and matched on 8 October. JODI reports refinery output to 2024 but is not used (8 October); it is shown as a comparison row only
analyst_proposal: Leave 2022 onward blank until the department publishes a balance or refiners give output by product (DR08)
